title: Profinite partition image incidence spaces reconstruct the pullback
statement:
Let $S,P$ be profinite spaces (compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected), let $X$ be any topological space, and let $f:S\to P$ and $g:X\to P$ be continuous. A finite clopen partition is a finite set of nonempty pairwise disjoint clopen subsets with union $S$; for empty $S$ it is empty. Let $I$ be the small nonempty directed poset of all such partitions, ordered by refinement. For $\mathcal Q\in I$ give its set of parts the discrete topology and put
$$Y_{\mathcal Q}=\{(x,A)\in X\times\mathcal Q:g(x)\in f(A)\}$$
with the subspace topology (equivalently, the disjoint union of $g^{-1}(f(A))$ over the parts). Refinement sends $(x,A')$ to $(x,A)$ for the unique containing part $A$. Give the set of compatible families $(y_{\mathcal Q})_{\mathcal Q\in I}$ the subspace topology in $\prod_{\mathcal Q}Y_{\mathcal Q}$, the topological inverse limit [def-kun-subspace-topology]. Writing $A_{\mathcal Q}(s)$ for the unique part containing $s$, the map
$$\{(x,s)\in X\times S:g(x)=f(s)\}\longrightarrow\varprojlim_{\mathcal Q\in I}Y_{\mathcal Q},\qquad(x,s)\longmapsto((x,A_{\mathcal Q}(s)))_{\mathcal Q}$$
(the left side with the subspace topology of the product $X\times S$ [def-kun-subspace-topology])
is a homeomorphism. More explicitly, a compatible choice of parts $(A_{\mathcal Q})$ has intersection $\{s\}$ for a unique $s\in S$, and $\bigcap_{\mathcal Q}f(A_{\mathcal Q})=\{f(s)\}$. The coordinate maps $S\to\mathcal Q$ generate its topology. The statement includes empty $S$ and empty $X$, with both sides empty in either case.

proof.text: Use Mathlib DiscreteQuotient S, a nonempty semilattice with top ordered from finer to coarser quotients. The explicit incidenceComparison uses ofLE_proj to give its compatibility. No nonemptiness assumption on S or X is introduced. For the final empty cases, the pullback is empty by either coordinate, and surjectivity of incidenceComparison then makes the incidence limit empty.

source.place: Preliminaries, directed partitions; *2.*, index and empty cases made explicit.

proof.text: Put e(s)(Q)=Q.proj s. Each coordinate is continuous, so e is continuous. Mathlib DiscreteQuotient.eq_of_forall_proj_eq makes e injective. Since S is compact and the product of the discrete quotients is Hausdorff, Continuous.isClosedEmbedding makes e an embedding. Its induced-topology equality expands using induced_iInf and induced_compose to give exactly the claimed infimum of induced quotient topologies. This replaces the explicit clopen-basis argument.

source.place: *2.*, “clopen partitions separate the points” and topology of the map to S; Topology Tag 08ZZ, lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering.

proof.text: For compatible a(Q), Mathlib DiscreteQuotient.exists_of_compat supplies s with Q.proj s=a(Q) for every Q. Mathlib DiscreteQuotient.eq_of_forall_proj_eq shows that a point in all the chosen fibres equals s. Conversely s belongs to every fibre. Therefore their intersection is {s}, and singleton injectivity gives uniqueness of the point with the two required intersection identities.

source.place: *2.*, “the A_Q have intersection a single point s, and every s arises”; Topology Tag 005D, lemma-intersection-closed-in-quasi-compact.

proof.text: For a fixed s, let p lie in every image f(Q.proj inverse({Q.proj s})). Define C_Q=f inverse({p}) intersect Q.proj inverse({Q.proj s}). These sets are closed by continuity, Hausdorff P and closed quotient fibres; they are compact as closed subsets of compact S, and nonempty by image membership. The quotient Q inf R refines both Q and R, and fiber_subset_ofLE with ofLE_proj makes the family downward directed. Apply the compact closed finite-intersection result, in the directed form IsCompact.nonempty_iInter_of_directed_nonempty_isCompact_isClosed, to obtain t in every C_Q. Equality of all projections gives t=s, hence p=f(s). Conversely f(s) lies in every image. This proves the image intersection identity, including for the compatible family of step 3.

source.place: *2.*, “Moreover” and the compact-fiber argument; Topology Tag 005D, lemma-intersection-closed-in-quasi-compact.

proof.text: The comparison is injective: read x from its top coordinate, and recover equality of s from all its quotient coordinates. For an incidence family y, apply exists_of_compat to its second coordinates, obtaining s. All first coordinates equal x=(y(top)).first by compatibility with top. Incidence and the image-intersection equality of step 4 give g(x)=f(s). The pair (x,s) maps back to y coordinatewise, proving surjectivity. Form the equivalence E from this proved bijectivity.

source.place: *2.*, compatible primes identified with pairs (x,s); explicit two-sided inverse.

proof.text: At each quotient Q the comparison is the subtype map induced by (x,s) mapping to (x,Q.proj s). Coordinate projections and Q.proj are continuous; continuous_pi and Continuous.subtype_mk give continuity into the product and then the compatible-family subtype. All subspaces carry the inherited topologies.

source.place: *2.*, continuity of the partition coordinates; product and incidence subspace topologies written out.

proof.text: The identity E(E inverse(y))=y gives both coordinate identities of its inverse. The inverse x coordinate is evaluation at top followed by subtype inclusion and first projection, hence continuous. After composition with the embedding e of step 2, the inverse s coordinate is, at every Q, evaluation at Q followed by subtype inclusion and second projection; continuous_pi proves this continuous. IsEmbedding.continuous_iff now gives continuity of the inverse s coordinate. Combining the coordinates and restricting to the pullback subtype gives a continuous inverse, hence a Homeomorph whose underlying function is incidenceComparison. No separation assumption on X is used.
